lead_headline: The Perfect Crumb cottage bakery surfaces in Thornton — subscriber net flatlines at zero for second time this week

restaurant.blurb: 1 new lead today: The Perfect Crumb cottage bakery (Elyria Swansea/Thornton) confirmed as home-based operation active at farmers markets and pop-ups across metro.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications for the thirteenth straight day as the state licensing freeze extends into its third week post-collapse with no system restoration timeline. The 7-day window flatlines at absolute zero versus last Wednesday's identical void, now marking 13 consecutive days since the April 29-30 renewal surge dumped 2,144 applications and froze the pipeline. No new filings, no status changes, no backend movement — the blackout persists across all license types with May's calendar remaining completely dark through mid-month. Backend system reconciliation appears structural rather than transactional as the workweek opens with zero visibility into queue restoration.

reputation.blurb: 6 mentions yesterday led by Denver Post HOA coverage and Colorado Blvd retail plans, lifting the 7-day total to 48 across 9 sources — up 17% from last week's 41 and 2% above the prior comparison window. Denver Post commands 44% share with 21 mentions, followed by Instagram (10) and scattered X/Facebook cross-posts. Google News RSS drives 98% of discoveries (47 of 48) as real estate and development stories sustain elevated pickup. Week-over-week momentum builds modestly heading toward mid-month, with the 48-mention floor establishing a new weekly baseline 17% ahead of last Wednesday's 41-mention benchmark.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +0 yesterday (1 new, 1 canceled) holds MTD at +16 (+1.3/day) while 90-day net advances to +136. Monday's balanced equation — matching acquisition with churn — follows Sunday's identical +1 net, compressing this week's momentum to +2 versus last week's +20. This week's softer +2 net (18 new, 16 canceled) runs 90% below last week's +20 (26 new, 6 canceled), with acquisition down 31% even as cancellations surge 167%. MTD's +1.3/day rate matches YTD baseline but masks recent volatility — the last 7 days show tighter conversion amid elevated churn. The pattern shifts from last week's strong acquisition/low-churn model to compressed inbound flow with retention pressure building through the month's second week.
